transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doc, I'm here because... I mean, my wife actually made the appointment, but I guess she's right. I keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I'm an operations manager, right? So I'm used to stress, used to putting out fires. But lately, I'm just snapping on these operations calls, biting people's heads off. And it's not just at work, it's at my family, too. Which is crazy, because I've never handled things like this. Usually, I'm the calm one. Speaking of calm, I used to go fishing down at Lake Mead to unwind. You ever been? Beautiful out there, especially early morning when the water is just like glass. I caught this massive bass there back in '19... or was it '18? My buddy Dave was there, he had this old truck that kept stalling on the way up... anyway, yeah, I'm just so irritable lately. It's like I have zero patience for anything.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like fishing or spending time with family?

Yeah, I haven't even touched my rods. I actually need to take my best reel into the shop, the drag is totally shot on it. You know how hard it is to find a good repair place nowadays? Everything is just buy-new, throw it away, nobody fixes anything. Used to be a guy off Route 9 who did it, but he closed up shop last year. 

But... yeah, with the family... it's just weird lately. Like, my wife will make a nice dinner, or the kids will be sitting around talking about soccer like normal. My youngest plays center forward, actually. And his coach, Greg—man, that guy takes it way too seriously. He's got these ten-year-olds running suicides in 90-degree heat. I told him last season he's gonna give someone heatstroke if he doesn't dial it back, but he thinks he's coaching the World Cup or something. 

Anyway, they'll be at the table talking about practice or whatever, and I know I should feel glad to just be there with them, right? I love my family. But it’s like... there’s just nothing in me that can respond. I just sit there, and I can't feel any of the good stuff I'm supposed to be feeling.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just irritable but actually sad or hopeless?

Sad? No, I wouldn't say sad. I'm not sitting around crying or feeling depressed all day. I mean, hopeless... the only thing hopeless right now is the supply chain at work, honestly. We've had these shipping containers sitting at the port for three weeks. Three weeks! And the port authority just drags their feet. My buddy Mike works down there, actually, driving one of those massive cranes—you know, the ones that load the freighters? He says the whole system is just a bureaucratic nightmare right now because they updated their logistics software back in April and it's been a total disaster ever since. Nobody knows where anything is, and the drivers are just sitting in their cabs for hours. 

But anyway... no, I don't feel depressed myself. Just... like I said, mostly just snapping at people, or just feeling kind of blank. Not sad, really.
Have you been feeling like nothing really brings you pleasure or satisfaction lately, even things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, that's exactly what I meant earlier when I was talking about the kids and dinner. It's like... I know I should feel good, or satisfied, or just happy to be sitting there with them, but I just can't feel it. 

Like the other night, my wife made this unbelievable smoked brisket. We got one of those pellet grills for the backyard last summer—man, it's a total game changer. You just load up the hopper with hickory or applewood pellets, set the temp, and it connects right to an app on your phone. Though, honestly, the Bluetooth range on the thing is absolute garbage. If I walk past the kitchen island, it loses connection, and I have to restart the whole app. I ended up having to buy a Wi-Fi extender just to get a signal out to the patio, which was a whole other headache to set up because our router is ancient. I keep telling the cable company to send us a new one, but you know how they are. 

But anyway... she makes this huge, great meal, the kids are laughing and having a good time, and I'm just sitting there chewing. I don't feel any joy from it, no pleasure at all. Just... nothing in me responds to it anymore.
Have you had days where you felt down or depressed most of the time, not just irritable or blank, and if so, how often has that happened over the past couple of weeks?

Like I said a minute ago, no, not really. I don't have days where I'm just down in the dumps or depressed. I mean, the only ones acting depressed lately are my warehouse guys because I had to mandate weekend shifts to clear out that backlog I was talking about. 

We just switched over to this new inventory management system too—corporate forced it on us, of course. The old scanner guns worked perfectly fine, but now everything is on these rugged tablets that weigh like five pounds each. Half the guys keep dropping them, and the screens crack, and then I'm the one who has to get on the phone with IT to order replacements. Have you ever tried getting a straight answer out of an IT department? It’s like pulling teeth. They submit a ticket, and it just goes into a black hole. Jimmy, my lead forklift driver, he actually ran over one of the tablets last Thursday. Just completely crushed it. He said it was an accident, but honestly, I think he did it on purpose because the interface is so terrible. It takes five clicks just to log a pallet now. 

But... yeah, no. To answer your question, I'm not sad. I haven't had any days like that. Just... like I said, empty. Or aggravated. But not depressed.
Have you felt unusually tired or noticed a loss of energy lately, even when you haven't been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Tired? I mean, yeah, I'm tired, but... who wouldn't be? I'm up half the night anyway. But it's not like a physical exhaustion, you know? It's just... I don't know. 

Speaking of physical exhaustion, though, my brother-in-law just signed up for one of those crazy Ironman triathlons. The guy is out of his mind. He's forty-five, hasn't worked out since college, and suddenly he's biking fifty miles on a Sunday morning. He bought this carbon-fiber road bike that cost more than my first car. Seriously, it weighs like twelve pounds. He let me pick it up at their barbecue last weekend, and it feels like holding a piece of cardboard. But the tires on those things are so thin, I don't know how they don't just snap on every pothole. And out where they live, the roads are terrible. The city was supposed to repave their subdivision three years ago, but the contractor went bankrupt halfway through the job, so now half the neighborhood is fresh asphalt and the other half looks like a war zone. 

But, uh... energy. Yeah, I don't know. I'm just... I wouldn't say I've lost energy for no reason. I'm just drained from everything going on.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or low—not just empty or irritable—but actually depressed, and if so, how often has that happened?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like, literally two minutes ago? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. No, I haven't been feeling depressed. I told you, I'm not sad, I'm just empty. Or aggravated. 

Aggravated is definitely the word. Like this morning, I stopped at the gas station on the corner of 4th and Elm—the one with the car wash attached. I just wanted a black coffee, right? Simple. But their machine was broken, just flashing some error code, so I had to wait in line for the cashier to make a fresh pot. And the guy in front of me is buying, I kid you not, fifty dollars worth of scratch-offs. Who buys fifty dollars of scratch-offs at 6:30 in the morning? And he's standing there scratching them right on the counter, holding up the whole line. The cashier didn't even say anything, just stood there staring at her phone. I swear, customer service is completely dead. 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I'm not depressed. Just... whatever this is.
Have you found it harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Focus? Uh, I mean... no, not really. I don't think so. I make decisions all day at the warehouse, that's my whole job. 

Though, honestly, trying to get anyone else to make a decision is the real problem. Like my wife, for instance. We were trying to figure out what to do with the gutters this weekend. They're completely backed up with leaves from that massive oak tree in the neighbor's yard. I told him last year he needed to trim those branches back because they hang right over our property line, but he's one of those guys who thinks his property is a nature preserve or something. He's got these bird feeders everywhere, which just attract squirrels. Dozens of them. They get into the attic, they chew on the wires... my buddy Dave had a squirrel chew through his main electrical line and it almost burned his whole house down. He had to live in a Marriott for three months while the insurance company dragged their feet. Have you ever stayed in a hotel for three months? The continental breakfast gets really old, really fast. 

But, uh, no. I'm thinking fine. Making decisions is fine. Just... normal stuff.
Have you felt like nothing really interests you or gives you any sense of enjoyment, even things you used to like doing, pretty much every day for the past couple of weeks?

Enjoyment? I mean... it's not that I don't care, it's just... I don't know how to explain it. Like, my wife will make dinner, or my kids will be at the table talking about their soccer games like normal, and I know I should feel glad to be there with them. I know I should be happy. But it’s like there’s nothing in me that can respond. It's just flat. 

Speaking of soccer, though, the league they play in is completely disorganized this year. They changed the age brackets, so now my youngest is playing against kids who are practically a foot taller than him. And the referees? Half of them are just high school kids who don't even pay attention to the game. Last week, one of them was literally texting on his phone while a kid got cleated in the shin. The parents were going crazy, yelling from the sidelines. One guy—I think he's a chiropractor over on Main Street—actually marched onto the field and started screaming at the ref. They had to stop the game for twenty minutes. It's ridiculous. You pay three hundred dollars for registration and they can't even hire real officials. 

But yeah, I don't know. Things just don't feel... good right now. Even when they should.
Have you had days where you felt down or low most of the time, not just empty or irritable, and if so, how often has that happened over the past couple of weeks?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like, literally a few minutes ago? I feel like we're going in circles here. No, I haven't been feeling depressed. I told you, I'm not sad, I'm just empty. Or aggravated. 

Aggravated is definitely the word. Like this morning, I stopped at the gas station on the corner of 4th and Elm—the one with the car wash attached. I just wanted a black coffee, right? Simple. But their machine was broken, just flashing some error code, so I had to wait in line for the cashier to make a fresh pot. And the guy in front of me is buying, I kid you not, fifty dollars worth of scratch-offs. Who buys fifty dollars of scratch-offs at 6:30 in the morning? And he's standing there scratching them right on the counter, holding up the whole line. The cashier didn't even say anything, just stood there staring at her phone. I swear, customer service is completely dead. 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I'm not depressed. Just... whatever this is.
Have you felt like you don’t care about doing things you used to enjoy, even things that were really important to you, like spending time with your kids or fishing?

Wait, I thought we just covered this. I swear, doc, you're asking the exact same things over and over. Didn't I just tell you about my kids at the dinner table? It's not that I don't care about them. I'm just... flat. 

And fishing? I haven't been fishing in months. Honestly, the lake we usually go to has been totally ruined lately. They built this new subdivision right up against the eastern shore, all these massive McMansions with three-car garages. And the runoff from their fertilized lawns is causing these huge algae blooms. It's disgusting. The water looks like pea soup by mid-July. My buddy Steve took his boat out there a few weeks ago and said the motor kept getting tangled in this thick green sludge. He spent two hours just trying to clean the prop when he got back to the dock. And the fish they're pulling out of there now? They look sick. I wouldn't eat anything out of that water if you paid me. The state DNR is supposed to be monitoring it, but you know how government agencies are. They'll probably do a study for five years and then tell us what we already know. 

But yeah, like I said before... I just don't feel anything right now. It's not about not caring. It's just... nothing.
Have you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, not just sometimes during the day but consistently, and if so, how often has that been happening lately?

I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. We just talked about this, didn't we? Are you reading off a list or something? Because I'm telling you again, no, I haven't been feeling down or depressed. I'm not sitting around crying. 

Speaking of sitting around, though, the guys down at the warehouse have been doing way too much of that lately. I manage the operations over at the distribution center on Route 9, and ever since they brought in this new inventory tracking software, everything has ground to a halt. The system is supposed to be "automated" and "streamlined," but it crashes every time someone scans a barcode too fast. So you've got forklift drivers just sitting there, twiddling their thumbs, waiting for the IT guy to reset the servers. And the IT guy? He works remotely from three states away. You have to put in a ticket and wait four hours just to get a response. Meanwhile, we've got trucks backed up to the highway waiting to unload. The drivers get pissed, the dispatchers are yelling at me, and corporate is sending these passive-aggressive emails about our metrics dropping. It's a total disaster. I told them six months ago we should stick with the old system, but nobody listens to the operations manager until the whole place catches on fire. 

But no, to answer your question again... I'm not feeling down or sad. Just... irritated. And empty. Like I said.
Have you felt like nothing you do is giving you any real pleasure or satisfaction lately, even things you used to really enjoy, like fishing or spending time with your kids?

Are you messing with me? Seriously, doc, are you just pressing a button that spits out the same question every two minutes? We literally just talked about this. Fishing, the kids... I just told you. 

But fine, I'll say it again. It's not that I don't care, it's that I can't feel anything good about it. Like, my wife will make dinner, or my kids will be sitting there talking about their soccer games like normal, and I know I should feel glad to be there with them. I should feel happy. But it’s like there’s nothing in me that can respond. It's just a blank wall. 

Speaking of soccer, though, you wouldn't believe the drama with my son's league this year. The parents have completely lost their minds. They brought in this new coach, this guy who used to play semi-pro or something, and he thinks he's managing a Premier League team. These kids are ten years old, and he's running them through these intense conditioning drills for two hours straight. Last week, one of the kids actually threw up on the sideline, and the coach just yelled at him to hydrate and get back on the field. The mom went ballistic, understandably, and started screaming at the coach right there in front of everyone. Then the referee got involved, and someone threatened to call the cops. Over a ten-year-old's soccer practice! It's ridiculous. The league fees went up by fifty bucks this season, too, and for what? To watch grown adults scream at each other while the kids stand around looking miserable. I swear, youth sports used to be about having fun, but now it's just this toxic, hyper-competitive racket. 

But yeah, back to what you were asking... I just don't get any satisfaction or happiness out of anything right now. It's just dead inside. Like I've been saying this whole time.
Have you had days where you felt down or low most of the time, not just empty or irritable, and if so, how often has that happened over the past couple of weeks?

Are you... are you doing a bit? Is this some kind of psychological test to see how long it takes before I snap? Because I'm pretty sure you just asked me that. Literally the exact same thing about feeling down or low. And I'm telling you again—no. I'm not sad. I'm not sitting around crying into my coffee. 

Speaking of coffee, though, the machine in the breakroom at work has been broken for three weeks. Three weeks! And the vending company they contract with is completely useless. They sent a guy out last Tuesday, and he just stood there staring at it, kicked the bottom panel, and said they needed to order a part from Germany. Germany! For a standard drip coffee maker. So now everyone is bringing in their own thermoses, or they're sneaking out to the drive-thru down the street, which takes twenty minutes because the line is always wrapped around the building. And the owner of that place? He just jacked up the prices again. Four dollars for a plain black coffee. It's extortion, is what it is. And the people at the warehouse are getting jittery and pissed off because they can't get their caffeine fix, so productivity is tanking even more than it was with the software issues. I tried to just buy a cheap Mr. Coffee for the office out of my own pocket, but HR said it was a "fire hazard" and violated company policy. A fire hazard! But sure, let the forklift drivers operate heavy machinery while they're going through caffeine withdrawal. That makes total sense.

But look, doc, I don't know how many ways I can say it. I don't feel sad or down. I'm just empty. Irritated, yeah, obviously. But not depressed. Can we please move on to something else?
Have you noticed that you have trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?

Concentrating? Making decisions? No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I can think just fine, when I'm not being asked the same question five times in a row, anyway. 

But you know what really requires concentration? Trying to get my lawnmower to start these days. It's this older John Deere riding mower, right? Good machine, usually reliable. But lately, the carburetor has been acting up. I spent four hours on Sunday just trying to clean the jets out. You have to take the whole side panel off, drain the gas line—which, by the way, gas is so expensive now, it physically hurts to spill even a drop of it on the driveway. Anyway, I get the whole thing apart, and I'm sitting there with a toothbrush and some carb cleaner, and my neighbor, Gary, comes over. Gary is one of those guys who thinks he knows everything about engines because he watched a couple of YouTube videos. He stands there over my shoulder, drinking a beer, telling me I'm adjusting the float valve wrong. I'm like, "Gary, I've had this mower since before you moved into this neighborhood, I think I know how the float valve works." But he just keeps talking, on and on about this zero-turn mower he's thinking about buying. Like I care about his landscaping dreams while I'm up to my elbows in grease. 

So yeah, my thinking is fine. No trouble making decisions. Just... trouble getting my mower to run without Gary breathing down my neck.
Have you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Are you... are you serious right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills. I literally just answered this. Like, two minutes ago! Did you not hear the whole thing about the coffee maker and the fire hazard? I said no. I am not feeling sad. I am not feeling down. It's not depression. I'm just empty. 

You know what is depressing, though? The price of groceries. I went to the store yesterday just to get some basics—milk, bread, a pack of chicken breasts—and it was like fifty bucks. Fifty! For almost nothing. And the checkout lines were insane because they only had two cashiers working. The rest were those self-checkout machines, which I swear are designed to torture people. The woman in front of me had a cart full of produce and couldn't figure out how to weigh the bananas. She just stood there poking the screen while the machine kept yelling, "Unexpected item in the bagging area!" over and over. I almost lost it. I ended up having to help her just so I could pay for my chicken and get out of there. And then I get out to the parking lot, and someone had left their cart right in the middle of the only empty space. People are just so inconsiderate these days, you know? Nobody cares about anyone else.

But no, doc. For the millionth time. I don't feel sad or low. I'm not depressed. Please, I am begging you, ask me something else.

But, uh... energy. Yeah, I don't know. I'm just... I wouldn't say I've lost energy for no reason. I'm just drained from everything going on.
